sets.title: Health
sets.scenario_prompt: As part of a university project, you have agreed to take part in a short research interview about health and wellness habits. A graduate student conducting the research will ask you some questions online.

tasks.question: Thank you for agreeing to participate. I'd like to ask you some questions about your health and wellness habits. First, do you have any specific routines or practices you use to maintain your physical wellbeing? If so, what are they?
model_responses: Yes, I have several routines that help me maintain my physical well-being. First, I make sure to drink at least two liters of water every day. Staying properly hydrated helps me feel more energetic and focused, especially when I have a busy schedule. I usually keep a water bottle beside me, so drinking water becomes an automatic habit rather than something I have to remember. Another routine is taking a thirty- to forty-minute walk with my friends about three times a week. Since I spend most of the day sitting at a desk, walking gives me a chance to stretch my legs, get some fresh air, and stay active. It is also a relaxing social activity. These simple habits are easy to maintain, but they make a noticeable difference to my overall health.
key_phrases: drink at least two liters of water every day
take a thirty- to forty-minute walk
spend most of the day sitting at a desk
get some fresh air and stay active
make a noticeable difference to my overall health

tasks.question: Thank you, can you describe any dietary choices or habits that you follow to stay healthy? Give details to extend your answer.
model_responses: One dietary habit I follow is eating a wide variety of foods. I try to include vegetables, fruit, meat, fish, and whole grains in my meals instead of relying on the same few dishes every day. This balanced approach allows me to obtain different vitamins, minerals, protein, and healthy fats, all of which are essential for normal body functions. Another habit is limiting my sugar intake. I rarely drink sugary beverages, and when I want a snack, I usually choose fruit or yogurt instead of candy. Consuming too much sugar can damage our teeth and may also contribute to weight gain and unstable blood sugar levels. I do not follow a strict diet, because that would be difficult to sustain. Instead, I focus on variety and moderation, which makes healthy eating more practical in the long run.
key_phrases: eat a wide variety of foods
be essential for normal body functions
be practical in the long run

tasks.question: Interesting. If you could make one significant change to your diet or exercise routine to stay healthy, what would it be? Why would you make that particular choice?
model_responses: If I could make one significant change to my diet, I would cook at home more often instead of ordering takeout. Because I have a busy work schedule, I currently rely on food delivery several times a week. Although it is convenient, restaurant food often contains more oil, salt, and sugar than I realize, and the portions can also be too large. By preparing my own meals, I could choose fresher ingredients, control the amount of seasoning, and create a better balance of vegetables, protein, and whole grains. To make this habit practical, I would plan simple meals on weekends and prepare some ingredients in advance. This change would not require a strict diet, but it would help me eat more nutritious food, manage my weight, and develop a healthier routine that I could maintain in the long run.
key_phrases: contain more oil, salt, and sugar
maintain a healthier routine in the long run

tasks.question: Great! Some people believe that mental health is just as important as physical health, and should be given equal attention. Do you agree or disagree with this viewpoint? Why?
model_responses: I definitely agree that mental health is just as important as physical health and deserves equal attention. The two are closely connected. When people feel persistently unhappy, anxious, or emotionally exhausted, they may lose the motivation to exercise, socialize, or even complete everyday tasks. As a result, their physical health can gradually decline as well. On the other hand, regular physical activity can improve mental well-being because exercise helps the body release chemicals associated with pleasure and relaxation. For example, even a short walk outdoors can reduce stress and lift someone's mood. If mental health problems are ignored for a long period of time, they may become more serious and harder to manage. Therefore, people should care for their minds and bodies together through exercise, sufficient rest, supportive relationships, and professional help when necessary.
key_phrases: reduce stress and lift someone's mood
care for the mind and body together

sets.title: Exercise Programs
sets.scenario_prompt: You have volunteered for a research study at your university about exercise programs. You will have a short online interview with a researcher. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for agreeing to participate. I'd like to ask you some questions about exercise programs. First, do you think exercising daily is important for good health? Why or why not?
model_responses: I think some form of daily exercise is important for good health, but it does not have to be intense. Regular physical activity keeps our bodies active, improves blood circulation, and reduces the health risks associated with a sedentary lifestyle. It can also support our mental health by lowering stress and helping us sleep better. For example, people who sit at a desk all day could take a thirty-minute walk, stretch at home, or ride a bicycle instead of doing a demanding workout. However, I do not think people should train hard every single day, because their muscles need time to recover. A balanced routine could include strength training or running on some days and lighter activities on others. The most important thing is to move consistently and choose an activity that is safe, enjoyable, and sustainable.
key_phrases: reduce the health risks associated with...

tasks.question: Thank you. Imagine you are going to recommend or create an exercise program for a friend or family member who does not currently exercise. What kind of exercise or fitness routine would you recommend? Why?
model_responses: For a friend who does not currently exercise, I would recommend a simple four-day routine based on walking and strength training. On three days each week, the friend could take a brisk thirty-minute walk. Walking requires no special skills or expensive equipment, so it is an easy way to build endurance. On one day, I would suggest a short home workout with movements such as squats, wall push-ups, and gentle stretching. These exercises can strengthen muscle groups without placing pressure on the body. I would keep each session short at first and gradually increase the duration or difficulty. This program would be suitable for a beginner because it is affordable, flexible, and easy to follow. More importantly, the gradual pace would reduce the risk of injury and prevent the friend from feeling overwhelmed.
key_phrases: be based on walking and strength training
require no special skills or equipment

tasks.question: Interesting. For that same friend or family member, what do you think might challenge them the most about a regular exercise program? How would you help them through this challenge?
model_responses: I think the greatest challenge would be staying consistent, especially when the friend does not see immediate results. Exercising may feel tiring and inconvenient, while improvements in strength or appearance can take weeks. This may cause the friend to lose motivation and return to an inactive lifestyle. To help, I would divide the program into small, achievable goals, such as completing three walks in one week or exercising for thirty minutes without stopping. I would also exercise with my friend once or twice a week, because having a workout partner creates accountability and makes the routine more enjoyable. Finally, we could track progress on a calendar and celebrate improvements in energy, sleep, and mood instead of focusing only on weight. These strategies would help the friend notice progress and turn exercise into a lasting habit.
key_phrases: turn exercise into a lasting habit

tasks.question: Great, some people believe that it is important to have some sort of reward after a good week of exercising. What do you think would be a good reward for the program you created, and why?
model_responses: I think a good reward would be a relaxing weekend activity, such as watching a movie, visiting a favorite café, or taking a short trip. The reward should be enjoyable but should not undo the healthy habits the exercise program is trying to build. For that reason, I would avoid using junk food as the main reward. A pleasant experience would give the friend something to look forward to after completing all four exercise sessions. It could also help them associate regular exercise with positive feelings instead of seeing it as a punishment. Occasionally, a useful fitness item, such as comfortable workout clothes or new headphones, could be another motivating reward. Overall, the best reward is affordable, meaningful, and connected to the person's interests, because a personal reward is more likely to keep them motivated.
key_phrases: use junk food as the main reward
have something to look forward to

sets.title: Art and Creativity
sets.scenario_prompt: You have volunteered for a research study at your university about people’s experiences with art and creativity. You will have a short online interview with a researcher. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for your participation. I'd like to learn about your experiences with art and creativity. Do you consider yourself to be a creative person? Why or why not?
model_responses: Yes, I consider myself a creative person, although my creativity is usually expressed through problem-solving rather than traditional art. When I face a complicated problem, I try to think outside the box instead of automatically following the same approach that everyone else uses. I often break the problem down into smaller parts and examine the basic mechanism behind each one. This helps me understand the real cause of the problem instead of only dealing with its surface effects. Then, I compare several possible solutions and look for one that is both practical and efficient. For example, at work, I may redesign a process rather than repeatedly fix the same small mistake. To me, creativity means seeing a familiar situation from a different angle and developing an original solution that genuinely improves the result.
key_phrases: break a problem down into smaller parts
see a situation from a different angle

tasks.question: Great. Some people think that learning about art is just as important as learning science or math. Do you agree or disagree? Why?
model_responses: I agree that learning art is just as important as learning science or math because these subjects develop different but equally valuable skills. Science and math teach students to reason logically and analyze evidence, while art develops concentration, observation, and imagination. For example, when students draw an object, they have to pay close attention to its shape, proportions, colors, and small details. This kind of focused observation can also help them study scientific diagrams or solve complex math problems more carefully. Art also encourages students to experiment and accept that one problem may have several possible answers. That flexibility is useful in science, where new discoveries often begin with an unusual question or idea. Therefore, art should not be treated as an optional subject. It complements academic learning and helps students become more patient, imaginative, and well-rounded thinkers.
key_phrases: develop different but equally valuable skills

tasks.question: Interesting. Some people believe that engaging in creative activities can improve mental well-being. Do you agree or disagree? Why?
model_responses: I agree that creative activities can improve mental well-being because they give people a safe way to express their thoughts and emotions. When someone is drawing, writing, or making music, the mind can wander freely without the usual pressure of deadlines or other people's expectations. The person can explore an idea through imagination and does not need to worry about finding one correct answer. This freedom often creates a sense of calm and helps reduce stress. For example, after a difficult day, spending half an hour sketching or writing in a journal can shift a person's attention away from work and toward something personally meaningful. Creative activities can also produce a sense of achievement when an idea becomes a finished piece. Most importantly, the process allows people to understand their feelings without fear of being judged by others.
key_phrases: provide a safe way to express...
feel pressure from other people's expectations

tasks.question: Good points. One final question. Do you think future schools will teach more art or less? What factors might influence this?
model_responses: I think future schools will teach more art, although the form of art education may change. In the digital age, students spend a great deal of time viewing videos, photographs, advertisements, and other visual content on social media. To understand and create this content effectively, they need visual literacy, artistic judgment, and a basic sense of design. Schools may therefore introduce more courses in digital illustration, photography, animation, or video production instead of focusing only on traditional painting. The job market will also influence this change, because many careers now combine technology with creative communication. However, school budgets and the importance placed on standardized tests may limit the amount of classroom time available for art. Overall, if educators and employers continue to value creativity and digital content skills, art will probably play a larger role in future education.
key_phrases: the form of art education may change
spend a great deal of time doing...
view visual content on social media
have a basic sense of design
limit the amount of classroom time
play a larger role in future education

tasks.question: Thank you. What genres or types of music do you usually enjoy listening to? For example, do you prefer classical, rock or jazz music? Give details to explain your answer.

have a passion for country music
escape the pressure of city life

combine relaxing images with emotional storytelling

What interests me most is the close relationship between the lyrics and the beat. Skilled rappers can deliver words in a precise rhythm, which makes the language itself feel like part of the music. In a live house, the audience stands close to the performer, follows the beat, dances, and responds to the music together. That kind of interaction would create an exciting atmosphere that a video cannot reproduce. I would prefer to go with friends because we could share the experience, dance without feeling awkward, and enjoy the powerful rhythm together.

the relationship between the lyrics and the beat
deliver words in a precise rhythm

tasks.question: Great. Some people believe that music can have a powerful effect on our emotions and moods. Do you agree or disagree with this viewpoint? Why?
model_responses: I definitely agree that music can have a powerful effect on our emotions because both its rhythm and lyrics can change the way we feel. For example, even when we are happy, a slow and emotional melody may make us feel sad. The song may remind us of a past relationship or another experience, bringing back memories. By contrast, music can also improve a negative mood. If I feel frustrated because I made a mistake in the morning, I may listen to an energetic hip-hop song whose message is that failure is not a big deal and that I should try again. The strong beat and encouraging lyrics can restore my confidence and give me the courage to continue. Therefore, music does more than entertain us; it can intensify, redirect, or completely transform our emotions.

listen to a slow and emotional melody

sets.title: Cultural Festivals
sets.scenario_prompt: You have volunteered for a research study at your university about cultural festivals. You will have a short online interview with a researcher. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for agreeing to participate. I'd like to ask you some questions about cultural festivals. First, cultural festivals are events that celebrate traditions like food, music, art, or clothing from a certain culture. Have you ever been to one? Or would you like to go to one? Why?
model_responses: Yes, I have attended a Dragon Boat Festival celebration, and it was an exciting cultural experience. I watched long boats decorated like dragons race across the water while the teams paddled rapidly to the beat of drums. The event felt like both a competitive sport and a traditional ceremony. I also tried making zongzi, which are sticky-rice dumplings wrapped in leaves. Folding the leaves correctly was much harder than it looked, but learning the process was fun. In the future, I would also love to attend Carnival in Brazil. The parades, costumes, music, and dancing always look colorful and full of energy. Experiencing the celebration in person would allow me to feel the local atmosphere and understand the culture through direct participation, rather than simply reading about it or watching it on a screen.
key_phrases: paddle to the beat of drums
be colorful and full of energy
understand a culture through direct participation

tasks.question: Thank you. If you were to go to a cultural festival, what would you like to see or do there?
model_responses: If I went to a cultural festival, tasting local food would be my top priority because food reveals much about people's everyday lives. For example, in Korea, foods such as kimchi and instant noodles are not simply tourist attractions; they are parts of daily meals. Trying them at a festival would make me feel as if I were tasting the culture instead of observing it from the outside. I would also like to participate in activities rather than only watch performances. For example, at a Halloween celebration, I could dress up in a costume, join a parade, or go trick-or-treating with local participants. Activities like these would help me understand how people experience the festival. Overall, I would combine food with active participation because using different senses makes a cultural experience more vivid and memorable.
key_phrases: understand how people experience a festival
make an experience vivid and memorable

tasks.question: Interesting, if you were to participate in a cultural festival for your own culture, what would you want to share with other people and why?
model_responses: At a festival celebrating Chinese culture, I would first share traditional Chinese food because it is diverse. Depending on the region, the flavors can be sweet, spicy, salty, or savory, so everyone could find something they enjoy. Food is also a natural icebreaker: people can taste a dish, discuss its ingredients, and learn the story behind it while eating together. I would also introduce hanfu, the traditional clothing worn during different periods of Chinese history. These clothes feature beautiful colors, flowing sleeves, and detailed patterns, and each style reflects the customs of a particular era. I would invite visitors to try on outfits and take photographs. Combining food with clothing would show that Chinese culture is not a single, uniform tradition. Instead, it includes many regional flavors, historical periods, artistic styles, and ways of life.
key_phrases: learn the story behind a dish
reflect the customs of a particular era
not be a single, uniform tradition
include many regional and historical differences

tasks.question: Great! Some people think cultural festivals are mainly just for fun, while others think they serve an important purpose, like helping to keep traditions alive. What do you think?
model_responses: I think cultural festivals serve both purposes, and their entertainment value helps keep traditions alive. On the one hand, festivals give people a break from work. They can enjoy food, watch performances, play games, and spend time with family. That enjoyment is valuable by itself. On the other hand, these activities pass cultural knowledge from one generation to the next. For example, during the Dragon Boat Festival, young people may eat zongzi, watch boat races, and hear the story associated with the holiday. If the festival disappeared, many of them might never learn why these customs matter. Because festivals are interactive and enjoyable, people absorb cultural knowledge without feeling as if they are attending a lesson. Therefore, fun and education are not competing goals; fun is what makes cultural traditions easier to remember and continue.
key_phrases: pass knowledge from one generation to the next
make traditions easier to remember and continue

sets.title: Hobbies
sets.scenario_prompt: You have volunteered for a research study at your university about hobbies. You will have a short online interview with a researcher. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for agreeing to participate. I'd like to ask you some questions about hobbies. To begin, do you have a hobby or interest that you regularly spend time doing?
model_responses: Yes, I have two hobbies that I regularly spend time on: learning foreign languages and playing the piano. Currently, I am learning Korean with a digital application called Duolingo. I practice for about fifteen minutes every day, which is short enough to fit into my schedule but still helps me make steady progress. The application uses games, points, and daily challenges, so the learning process feels motivating rather than stressful. It also allows me to practice vocabulary, grammar, listening, and pronunciation in one place. My other hobby is playing the piano after work. Unlike language learning, which requires concentration, playing familiar songs helps me clear my mind and relax. These two hobbies serve different purposes: Korean gives me a sense of progress and achievement, while the piano provides an enjoyable break from my daily responsibilities.
key_phrases: provide a break from daily responsibilities

tasks.question: Thank you. If you were to select a new hobby, what would you choose and why?
model_responses: If I selected a new hobby, I would choose programming, especially machine learning or deep learning. In today's digital world, knowledge of programming and artificial intelligence is becoming useful in almost every industry. These skills can help people automate tasks, analyze information more efficiently, and turn their ideas into practical tools. I would begin with a beginner-friendly language such as Python and complete projects instead of studying theory alone. For example, I might build a program that organizes my work materials or summarizes information. Eventually, I would like to explore how machine learning could support my work and help me discover possibilities that I cannot see now. Programming would be both an interesting intellectual challenge and a practical investment because it could strengthen my problem-solving ability, improve my efficiency, and expand my future career options.
key_phrases: be useful in almost every industry

tasks.question: Interesting. Now tell me what might prevent you from starting this new pastime.
model_responses: The factor that might prevent me from learning programming is a lack of time. Even if I am awake for sixteen hours a day, half of that time is spent working. The remaining hours must be divided among meals, responsibilities, rest, family, and friends. I also want to maintain my hobbies, including studying Korean and practicing the piano. Programming would require more than a few minutes of casual practice because I would need to understand concepts, write code, and solve technical problems regularly. reserve two fixed sessions each week

tasks.question: Great. Some people believe it is better to have one interest outside of work or school that you dedicate yourself to rather than multiple smaller ones. Do you agree or disagree? Why?
model_responses: I agree that dedicating yourself to one hobby is better than dividing your attention among many smaller interests. Focusing on one activity gives you time to move beyond the basic level and develop real skill. That progress can build confidence and may even create opportunities. For example, if I become highly proficient in Korean, I could use the language while traveling, communicate with more people, or teach students. In that way, a personal interest could eventually become a source of income or even part of a career. By contrast, if I constantly switch among several hobbies, I may understand the basics of each one without becoming good at any of them. Smaller hobbies are still useful for relaxation, but I believe having one central interest creates a stronger sense of direction, achievement, and long-term growth.

develop a high degree of skill
create a sense of long-term growth

key_phrases: release stress after a busy day
be easy to watch in a group
connect with current interests and experiences

tasks.question: I see. When you watch a movie, do you prefer to watch after work or school on weekdays or do you like to watch during the weekends? Why?

become completely absorbed in a film

model_responses: I do not have a garden, but I take care of one small succulent on my bedroom windowsill. I usually spend time on it only once a week because high school students have busy schedules. Most weekdays are filled with classes, homework and test preparation, so I cannot manage plants that require daily attention. On Sunday, I check whether the soil is dry, remove any damaged leaves and rotate the pot so that each side receives enough sunlight. The entire routine takes less than ten minutes. I chose a succulent because it stores water and can remain healthy even if I occasionally forget to care for it. Although I garden infrequently, the plant makes my room feel more pleasant and gives me a simple responsibility outside schoolwork. A low-maintenance plant is therefore a realistic choice for my current schedule.
key_phrases: take care of one small succulent
spend time on it once a week
check whether the soil is dry
be realistic for my current schedule

tasks.question: Thank you! What kinds of plants or gardens have you seen or heard about that you found interesting or appealing? Describe them and talk about why you found them interesting or appealing.
model_responses: One garden I find appealing is the small garden beside a school science building. It contains colorful flowers, several fruit trees and a vegetable area where students grow tomatoes, beans and herbs. Each class takes responsibility for a different section, and labels beside the plants explain their names and growing conditions. I find this kind of garden interesting for two reasons. First, it makes the school environment more attractive and gives students a peaceful place to relax during breaks. Second, it turns science lessons into practical experiences. Students can observe how seeds develop, compare different growing conditions and learn where food comes from. They also practise teamwork by watering plants and removing weeds together. A school garden is appealing because it combines nature, education and cooperation in a place that students already visit every day.
key_phrases: create a peaceful place during breaks

tasks.question: Interesting! What challenges do you think people face when trying to grow plants or maintain a garden?
model_responses: People face two main challenges when maintaining a garden. The first is providing the correct amount of light and water. Different plants have different needs, and beginners may water everything according to the same schedule. Too much water can damage roots, while too little sunlight can prevent healthy growth. The second challenge is maintaining the routine over time. People may forget to water plants during busy school or work periods, and traveling creates an additional problem. Weather, insects and plant diseases can also require quick attention. To handle these difficulties, gardeners can begin with low-maintenance plants, read care instructions and use reminders on their phones. They can also ask a friend to help when they are away. Successful gardening requires knowledge and consistency, so starting with a few suitable plants is more practical than creating a large garden immediately.
key_phrases: require different amounts of light and water

tasks.question: Great! Some people believe that gardening can have positive effects on personal mental health and well-being. Do you agree or disagree with this viewpoint? Why?
model_responses: I agree that gardening improves mental health and well-being for two reasons. First, it helps people reduce stress. Watering plants, touching the soil and spending time outdoors can shift attention away from homework or work-related worries. The activity is quiet and does not involve screens, so it gives the mind a useful break. Second, gardening creates a sense of achievement. Plant growth is gradual, but small changes such as a new leaf or flower show that regular effort produces a result. This can make people feel responsible and capable. For example, a student who successfully grows herbs on a balcony can use them in a family meal and feel proud of the contribution. Therefore, gardening supports well-being by creating a peaceful routine and providing visible evidence of progress over time.

sets.title: Friendship
sets.scenario_prompt: You have volunteered for a research study about people's experiences with friendship. You will have a short online interview with a researcher. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for signing up for the study. I'd like to ask you some questions about your experiences with friendship. First, do you have a large group of friends, or do you prefer to have a smaller group of friends?
model_responses: I prefer having a smaller group of close friends. I know many classmates and enjoy talking with them at school, but I regularly spend time with only four or five people. A small group works better for me for two reasons. First, it allows us to have meaningful conversations. In a large gathering, people often exchange only a few sentences, while close friends can discuss school pressure, family problems or future plans honestly. Second, a smaller group is easier to maintain. We can find time to eat together, study or play sports without coordinating dozens of schedules. I also have enough time to listen carefully and support each person when necessary. For me, friendship is based on trust and shared experience rather than the number of contacts on a phone, so a few close friends are enough.
key_phrases: prefer a smaller group of friends
value trust over the number of contacts

tasks.question: Very good. Now describe a time when a friendship taught you something valuable or helped you see something from a new perspective.
model_responses: One valuable experience happened during a group science project. I wanted our presentation to include as much information as possible, so I created many detailed slides. A close friend on my team told me that the presentation was difficult to follow and suggested using fewer words and more diagrams. At first, I felt disappointed because I had spent a long time collecting the information. Instead of rejecting the advice, I asked her to explain which parts were unclear. We redesigned several slides together, practised the presentation and received positive feedback from our teacher. The experience taught me that honest criticism can be a form of support. A good friend does not always agree with me; sometimes that person helps me recognize a weakness that I cannot see myself. Listening to a different perspective improved both the project and our friendship.
key_phrases: ask someone to explain the concern
see criticism as a form of support

tasks.question: Great. Next question. In your opinion, what makes a friendship last a long time?
model_responses: I think two qualities make a friendship last: honest communication and consistent effort. First, friends need to express their feelings and discuss problems directly. Misunderstandings become more serious when people remain silent or complain to others. A calm conversation gives both people a chance to explain their intentions and find a solution. Second, friendships require regular attention. Even close friends can gradually become distant if they never communicate or spend time together. Simple actions, such as sending a message, remembering an important event or meeting for lunch, show that the relationship still matters. For example, friends who attend different schools can schedule a monthly activity and share updates during the week. Long-lasting friendship does not require daily contact, but it does require trust, communication and repeated efforts from both people rather than only one person.

tasks.question: OK, last one. Some people believe that maintaining friendships is essential for emotional well-being and life satisfaction. Do you agree or disagree with this viewpoint? Why or why not?
model_responses: I agree that maintaining friendships is essential for emotional well-being for two reasons. First, friends provide emotional support during stressful periods. Students can talk about examination pressure or personal problems with someone who listens without judging them. Sharing worries often makes the situation feel more manageable and reduces loneliness. Second, friendship makes daily life more enjoyable. Studying, exercising or attending an event with friends can turn an ordinary activity into a positive memory. Friends may also encourage one another to try new experiences and continue difficult goals. For example, a student is more likely to maintain an exercise routine when a friend joins and provides motivation. Therefore, friendships improve life satisfaction by giving people both dependable support during difficult moments and enjoyable companionship during ordinary ones. Regular communication is necessary to preserve these benefits over time.

sets.title: Shopping Habits
sets.scenario_prompt: You have signed up for a study run by a university research group that is investigating shopping habits. You will have a short video interview with one of the researchers. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me. I'd like to ask you some questions about your shopping habits. When was your last shopping trip? And what did you buy? Did you have a good shopping experience?
model_responses: My last shopping trip was last Saturday, when I went to a shopping mall with my mother. I needed a new pair of sports shoes because my old ones had become uncomfortable and worn out. Before leaving home, I checked several models online and set a price limit. At the store, I tried on three pairs, walked around in each one and asked an employee about the materials and return policy. I chose a comfortable pair that was on sale and stayed within my budget. The experience was good because the store was organized and the employee gave useful advice without pressuring me to buy the most expensive option. Afterward, my mother and I had lunch together. The trip allowed me to make a careful purchase while also spending enjoyable time with a family member.

tasks.question: I see. When you shop, which do you like better: shopping for yourself or shopping for others? Why?
model_responses: I prefer shopping for myself for two reasons. First, I understand my own needs and preferences. I know which colors, sizes and features I will actually use, so I can make a decision without guessing. When buying sports shoes, for example, I can try them on and immediately judge whether they are comfortable. Second, shopping for myself makes budgeting easier. I can set a price limit, compare several options and decide whether the purchase is important enough to use my savings. Buying a gift for someone else is more uncertain because the person may already own the item or dislike the style. I still enjoy giving gifts on special occasions, but everyday shopping is less stressful when I know exactly what the buyer needs. Therefore, I prefer shopping for myself because it is more efficient and predictable.

tasks.question: Interesting. Next, I'd like to get your opinion. In recent years, people's shopping preferences have shifted in various ways. Do you think that in the future, people will continue to change how and where they shop? Why or why not?
model_responses: I believe people will continue to change how and where they shop for two reasons. First, technology will make shopping faster and more personalized. Applications can recommend products, compare prices and allow customers to purchase items from home. Services such as same-day delivery and automatic pickup lockers will make online shopping useful for even more products. Second, environmental concerns will influence consumer choices. More people may choose secondhand goods, reusable packaging or stores that sell locally produced items. For example, a student might compare a new textbook with a less expensive used copy before ordering. Businesses will respond by combining physical stores, websites and recycling services. Shopping preferences will therefore continue changing because consumers want greater convenience while also becoming more aware of cost and environmental impact. Companies that adapt to both needs will attract more customers.
key_phrases: use same-day delivery and pickup lockers

tasks.question: Good points. I just have one more question. Some people believe that buying too many products you do not need harms the environment. Do you agree with this idea? Why or why not?
model_responses: I agree that buying unnecessary products harms the environment for two reasons. First, manufacturing each product consumes natural resources and energy. Clothing, electronics and plastic items require raw materials, factory production and transportation, all of which can create pollution. If a product is rarely used, those environmental costs provide little value. Second, unnecessary purchases create more waste. Cheap or unwanted items may be thrown away after a short period, and packaging adds even more rubbish to landfills. Electronic products can be especially harmful because they contain materials that require special recycling. Consumers can reduce the problem by waiting before purchasing, choosing durable products and avoiding excessive packaging. Therefore, buying only what we genuinely need protects personal finances while reducing resource use, pollution and the amount of waste communities must manage.
key_phrases: buy only what we genuinely need

sets.title: Volunteering and Community Service

tasks.question: Thank you for agreeing to participate. I'd like to ask you some questions about your experiences with volunteering and community service. First, have you ever participated in any volunteer activities, and if you do, how often do you volunteer?
model_responses: Yes, I participate in volunteer activities several times each school year. Most opportunities are organized by my school, so I usually volunteer once or twice each semester. I prefer activities with a clear task because I can see how my time contributes to the result. During a park cleanup, my group collected litter and separated recyclable materials, making the area noticeably cleaner within a few hours. Volunteering also gives me a chance to work with classmates outside the classroom and communicate with people I might not normally meet. I cannot volunteer every week because of homework and examinations, but participating several times a year is realistic and helps me remain connected to my community.

tasks.question: Thank you. Can you tell me about a charity effort or a donation drive that you have heard about that made an impact on where you live?
model_responses: One school charity week in my community combined a book donation drive with a bake sale for a children's hospital. Students and families donated children's books, dictionaries and learning materials they no longer needed. Volunteers checked the books, sorted them by reading level and sent them to schools with limited resources. On another day, students baked cookies and cakes, sold them during lunch and donated the money to help young patients at a local hospital. The campaign made an impact because everyone could contribute in a different way. Some people donated books, some prepared food, and others designed posters or bought a snack. The event showed that simple school activities can produce meaningful results when many people contribute their time, skills or small donations.
key_phrases: raise money for a children's hospital

tasks.question: Interesting. Can you describe a public service project that you have been involved in or would like to participate in if you had the time?
model_responses: If I had time, I would participate in a community recycling project. Volunteers could first collect paper, plastic bottles, metal cans and food packaging from a park or neighborhood. We would then put the different materials into different colored bins, making the sorting process clear and easy to remember. To involve children, I would turn part of the activity into a game. Teams could identify each type of waste and race to place it in the correct bin. The most accurate team could receive a small environmentally friendly prize. This project would create two benefits. It would make the public space cleaner immediately, and it would teach residents how to sort waste correctly in daily life. The long-term goal would be to change behavior so that less recyclable material is placed in ordinary garbage.
key_phrases: participate in a community recycling project
turn waste sorting into a game

tasks.question: Great. Some people believe that volunteering should be a mandatory part of the school curriculum to help students develop a sense of community. Do you agree or disagree with this idea? Why?
model_responses: I disagree that volunteering should be mandatory for two reasons. First, high school students already have busy schedules filled with classes, homework and examinations. A fixed service requirement could create additional pressure or reduce the time available for academic subjects and rest. Second, students can develop community awareness through many other activities. Group projects, environmental clubs, donation drives and optional recycling programs all teach responsibility, communication and teamwork. Volunteering is also more meaningful when students choose a cause they genuinely care about. Someone interested in education may join a book drive, while another student may prefer a community cleanup or hospital bake sale. Schools should provide a variety of opportunities and actively encourage participation instead of forcing everyone to complete the same requirement. This flexible approach protects students' time while allowing genuine interest to develop.
key_phrases: choose a cause students genuinely care about

sets.title: Personal Goals and Achievements

tasks.question: Thank you for agreeing to participate. I'd like to ask you some questions about your personal goals and achievements. First, do you currently have any specific personal goals you are working towards? Give details to explain your answer.
model_responses: One personal goal I am working toward is becoming more confident at speaking English. I can understand reading materials, but I sometimes become nervous and speak too quickly during presentations. My specific target is to deliver a three-minute response clearly without reading a complete script. To reach it, I practise for fifteen minutes four times a week. I choose a familiar topic, organize two main ideas and record myself on my phone. Afterward, I listen for problems with my pace, pronunciation and sentence structure. I also ask a classmate or teacher for feedback once a week. I hope to achieve noticeable improvement before the end of the semester. This goal matters because stronger speaking skills will help me participate in class, communicate with more people and feel better prepared for future study opportunities.

tasks.question: Thank you. Can you describe some steps you can take to achieve these goals, or to achieve goals in general? What are the challenges you face when taking these steps?
model_responses: To achieve a goal, I follow three main steps. First, I turn a general intention into a measurable target. Instead of saying that I want better English, I decide to practise speaking for fifteen minutes four times a week. Second, I create a schedule and divide the goal into small tasks, such as learning useful expressions, recording a response and reviewing mistakes. Third, I track progress and ask for feedback so I can adjust the method. The greatest challenge is consistency. Homework, examinations and school activities sometimes make me feel too busy to practise. Another difficulty is discouragement when improvement is slow. I handle these problems by keeping each session short and recording completed tasks on a calendar. Small, visible progress makes the goal less overwhelming and helps me continue even when motivation is low.
key_phrases: turn an intention into a measurable target
divide the goal into small tasks

tasks.question: Interesting, can you describe an accomplishment that holds special meaning for you? What did you achieve and why is it significant to you?
model_responses: One accomplishment that holds special meaning for me was completing a science presentation with my classmates. Our topic was plastic pollution, and we needed to research the problem and recommend realistic solutions. At first, our information was disorganized and group members had different opinions about the presentation. I suggested dividing the work according to our strengths. One student collected statistics, another designed the slides and I organized the main argument and delivered part of the presentation. We met twice to compare our work and practise together. On presentation day, we explained our ideas clearly and answered the teacher's questions successfully. The project received one of the highest scores in the class. It was significant because I learned that a strong result depends not only on individual knowledge but also on communication, preparation and effective teamwork.

tasks.question: Great, some people believe that setting and working towards individual goals is crucial for self-improvement and personal growth. Do you agree or disagree with this idea? Why?
model_responses: I agree that individual goals are crucial for personal growth for two reasons. First, goals provide clear direction. Without a specific target, people may spend time on many activities without knowing which one deserves priority. A student who decides to practise English speaking four times a week knows exactly what action to take. Second, goals develop self-discipline and confidence. Following a plan requires effort even when motivation is low, and completing each small step creates visible progress. For example, comparing speaking recordings over several weeks can show improvements that are difficult to notice from day to day. This evidence encourages the student to continue and attempt more difficult tasks. Therefore, setting and pursuing goals helps people organize their effort, recognize their abilities and gradually become more independent and confident learners.

sets.title: Sleep Habits
sets.scenario_prompt: You have volunteered for a research study about sleep habits. You will have a short online interview with a researcher. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for your time. I'd like to ask you some questions about your sleep habits. First, do you usually go to bed early or late?
model_responses: I usually go to bed fairly early on school nights, at around ten thirty or eleven. I need to wake up before seven, so this schedule gives me approximately eight hours of sleep. Going to bed early helps me concentrate during morning classes and prevents me from feeling exhausted in the afternoon. I try to finish homework before ten and avoid starting a television program or game late at night. On weekends, I sometimes stay awake until midnight because I have more free time to watch a movie or talk with friends. However, I avoid changing my schedule too dramatically because sleeping very late makes Monday morning difficult. Overall, I prefer an early and consistent bedtime. It gives me enough energy for school, exercise and other activities while making it easier to wake up without feeling rushed.
key_phrases: get approximately eight hours of sleep
avoid starting activities late at night

tasks.question: Okay, thanks. What is your typical routine before bedtime? What do you usually do before going to bed?
model_responses: My bedtime routine begins about thirty minutes before I want to sleep. First, I finish any urgent homework and prepare my schoolbag and clothes for the next morning. This prevents me from worrying that I have forgotten something. Then, I wash, brush my teeth and fill a bottle of water for the next day. I put my phone on silent and leave it on a desk instead of taking it to bed. For the final fifteen minutes, I usually read a few pages of a novel or listen to quiet music. I avoid short videos because one video can easily turn into thirty minutes of scrolling. Following the same sequence each night tells my body that the day is ending. The routine helps me relax, fall asleep more quickly and begin the next morning in an organized way.
key_phrases: begin my routine thirty minutes before bed

tasks.question: Great. Now, some people have trouble sleeping when they stay overnight at a hotel or at a friend's house. Are you able to sleep well in unfamiliar places? Why or why not?
model_responses: I usually have difficulty sleeping well in an unfamiliar place. The first reason is that the environment feels different. A hotel may have an unfamiliar mattress, hallway noise or light coming through the curtains, so I notice sounds and sensations that I would ignore at home. The second reason is that my normal bedtime routine may be interrupted. When staying with a friend, people may talk later than usual, and I may not have the same quiet space for reading. To make sleeping easier, I bring earplugs and an eye mask when I travel. I also try to follow my normal schedule, avoid caffeine in the evening and spend a few minutes reading before bed. These familiar actions help me relax, although the first night in a new place is rarely as comfortable as sleeping at home.
key_phrases: have difficulty sleeping in unfamiliar places
bring earplugs and an eye mask
feel less comfortable than at home

tasks.question: Many parents worry about their teenage children getting enough sleep. Some high schools have considered starting later in the morning to allow teenage students more time to sleep each night. What do you think of this idea? Explain why.
model_responses: I support later high-school start times for two reasons. First, more sleep can improve students' concentration and academic performance. A tired student may struggle to follow an explanation, remember information or participate in discussion, even when the lesson is well designed. Starting later would allow teenagers to arrive more alert and use classroom time effectively. Second, sufficient sleep supports physical and mental health. Students who regularly sleep too little may feel irritable, stressed and too exhausted to exercise after school. An additional hour in the morning could help them maintain a healthier routine. Schools would need to adjust transportation and activity schedules, but these practical changes are worthwhile. A later start does not reduce learning time; it helps students make better use of that time by attending class with more energy, attention and emotional balance.

use self-study periods according to urgency

key_phrases: a recent trip I took was...

tasks.question: I see. One important part of traveling is deciding to go alone or with a group. Thinking about a place you would like to visit, would you prefer to go there alone or with a group? Why?
model_responses: I would prefer to visit Japan with a small group of friends for two reasons. First, traveling with others feels safer in an unfamiliar country. If we misunderstand a train route, lose an item or face another unexpected problem, several people can discuss the situation and find a solution together. Second, a group can divide responsibilities and save time. One friend can compare hotels, another can research transportation and someone else can find restaurants or cultural attractions. This makes planning less stressful for everyone. I would keep the group small, perhaps three or four people, so making decisions would still be easy. Sharing activities such as trying local food, visiting historical sites and taking photographs would also make the journey more enjoyable. A small group therefore provides both practical support and memorable shared experiences.
key_phrases: feel safer in an unfamiliar country

tasks.question: Interesting. For many people, one of the most exciting parts of travel is choosing a destination. If you are going to select a place to travel, how would you go about making a list of potential places? Please describe your process.
model_responses: I use a four-step process to create a list of possible destinations. First, I decide what type of experience I want, such as natural scenery, historical sites or local food. Second, I search travel websites, videos and recommendations from friends for places that match that interest. I write down five or six options instead of choosing immediately. Third, I compare practical factors, including transportation costs, accommodation, weather and the amount of time available. This helps me remove destinations that are too expensive or difficult to reach. Finally, I narrow the list to two or three places and discuss them with the people who may travel with me. We compare the main advantages and choose the option that fits everyone's schedule and budget. This process keeps the decision organized while allowing the group to consider both interests and practical limits.
key_phrases: decide what type of experience I want

tasks.question: Good points. Finally, one major issue with travel today is overcrowding. Popular places have so many tourists visiting at one time that the sites are unable to allow all the people to visit who want to. As a result, virtual travel experiences are becoming more common compared to real life travel. Do you think a virtual travel experience is worthwhile? Why or why not?
model_responses: I do not think virtual travel is a worthwhile replacement for real travel for two reasons. First, it cannot reproduce a complete sensory experience. A screen may show a beach or market, but viewers cannot feel the weather, taste local food or hear the natural sounds in the same way. Second, virtual travel lacks genuine human interaction. Visiting another place gives travelers opportunities to ask residents questions, practise another language and observe how people live in daily situations. These experiences broaden people's horizons more effectively than watching images alone. Virtual tours can provide useful information before a trip or allow someone to see an inaccessible site, but they do not achieve the main purpose of travel. Real travel remains more valuable because it combines physical surroundings, spontaneous events and direct cultural communication.

sets.title: Dining Preferences
sets.scenario_prompt: You have volunteered for a research study at your university about dining preferences. You will have a short online interview with a researcher. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for agreeing to participate. I'd like to ask you some questions about your dining preferences. First, how often do you eat out at restaurants? Do you do this daily, weekly, monthly, or less often?
model_responses: I usually eat at a restaurant once during the weekend. From Sunday evening to Friday evening, I stay at my boarding school, so I eat most weekday meals in the school cafeteria. The cafeteria is convenient and offers several choices, but eating there every day can feel repetitive. After returning home on Friday, I sometimes go out with my family or meet friends for a meal on Saturday. We may choose a restaurant to celebrate finishing an examination, talk about the week or simply enjoy food that is unavailable at school. Before deciding, we compare prices, locations and menu options in a group chat. Eating out once a week gives me a pleasant change from cafeteria meals and time to reconnect with people outside school. It is frequent enough to be enjoyable without becoming too expensive.
key_phrases: eat out once during the weekend
eat weekday meals in the cafeteria
take a break from repetitive meals
compare choices in a group chat

tasks.question: Thank you. If you were going to eat out, what types of cuisine do you prefer? For example, do you like savory foods or desserts?
model_responses: When I eat out, I prefer savory Chinese food because different regions offer very different flavors and cooking styles. For example, Sichuan cuisine is known for spicy dishes, while Cantonese food often uses lighter seasoning to emphasize fresh ingredients. Northern restaurants may serve dumplings and noodles, while other places specialize in fish, rice or local vegetables. I enjoy ordering several dishes for the table because everyone can compare flavors and share the experience. I am also interested in innovative versions of traditional food. A restaurant might keep the basic ingredients of a classic dish but change its presentation, add a new filling or use a healthier cooking method. These creative dishes feel modern without completely losing their cultural background. Overall, regional Chinese cuisine gives me both variety and tradition, while innovative dishes make familiar food more surprising and appealing.
key_phrases: offer different flavors and cooking styles
create innovative versions of traditional food

tasks.question: Interesting. Can you tell me about a memorable dining experience or meal you or a friend have had recently? What made it special or stand out?
model_responses: One memorable dining experience was my own birthday meal with several close friends. Because we normally stay at school during the week, we arranged the dinner for Saturday at a Chinese restaurant. My friends ordered dishes that everyone could share, and the restaurant served me a bowl of longevity noodles. In Chinese culture, the long noodles represent a long and healthy life, so the dish made the celebration feel connected to tradition. My friends had also contacted the restaurant in advance and asked the staff to prepare a cake without telling me. After the main meal, the lights were lowered, the cake appeared and everyone sang together. What made the dinner meaningful was the care behind these details. The noodles represented a traditional birthday wish, while the unexpected cake showed that my friends had spent time planning something especially for me.
key_phrases: celebrate my own birthday with friends
arrange the meal for the weekend
serve a bowl of longevity noodles
represent a long and healthy life
prepare a surprise cake in advance

tasks.question: Great. Some people believe that the atmosphere and service at a restaurant are just as important as the food quality. Do you agree or disagree with this viewpoint? Why?
model_responses: I agree that atmosphere and service are as important as food quality for two reasons. First, the atmosphere affects whether customers can relax and enjoy the meal. Even excellent food is difficult to appreciate in a dirty, noisy or uncomfortable room. Appropriate lighting, clean tables and enough space allow people to talk without feeling rushed. Second, good service solves problems and makes the experience smoother. Staff members can explain unfamiliar dishes, respond to allergies, correct an order and serve food at a suitable pace. During a family celebration, thoughtful employees can also help with a cake or seating arrangements. Customers visit restaurants for an experience, not only for calories. Therefore, food may attract people initially, but a comfortable atmosphere and reliable service determine whether they feel satisfied and want to return.
key_phrases: be as important as food quality

sets.title: Food and Nutrition
sets.scenario_prompt: As part of a university project, you have agreed to take part in a short research interview about food and nutrition. A graduate student conducting the research will ask you some questions online.

tasks.question: Thank you for agreeing to participate. I'd like to ask you some questions about your food and nutrition habits. First, do you follow any specific diet or eating plan?
model_responses: I do not follow a strict diet, but I use a simple balanced-eating plan. For most meals, I try to include vegetables or fruit, a source of protein and a carbohydrate such as rice, bread or noodles. I normally eat three meals a day and avoid skipping breakfast because it helps me concentrate during morning classes. I also limit sugary drinks and choose water or milk instead. My plan allows occasional snacks and desserts, so it does not feel like a punishment. I think strict rules would be difficult to maintain during family meals, school events or holidays. Instead, I focus on variety, reasonable portions and habits that can continue over time. This flexible approach gives me enough energy for school and exercise while allowing me to enjoy food without feeling guilty about every choice.

tasks.question: Thank you. Can you describe some foods that you eat on a regular basis?
model_responses: I regularly eat rice, vegetables, eggs, chicken, fruit and dairy products. Breakfast is usually simple, such as an egg with bread and milk or yogurt. For lunch and dinner, my family often prepares rice with two or three dishes. These may include leafy vegetables, tomatoes, chicken, fish or tofu. I try to eat fruit such as apples or bananas every day because it is convenient to carry to school. When I need a snack, I normally choose yogurt, nuts or fruit instead of candy. I also drink water throughout the day and rarely buy sugary beverages. The exact dishes change, but these basic foods appear regularly because they are affordable, easy to prepare and provide a useful balance of protein, carbohydrates, vitamins and healthy fats for school and physical activity.

tasks.question: Interesting. Tell me about a time when you or someone you know made a significant change to their diet. What was the change and what motivated you or the person you know to make it?
model_responses: A friend of mine made a significant change by replacing sugary drinks with water and unsweetened tea. She used to buy soda or milk tea almost every afternoon after school. The habit seemed harmless, but she often felt tired later and realized that the drinks also used a large part of her weekly allowance. Her main motivation was to feel more energetic and save money. She began carrying a reusable water bottle and allowed herself one sweet drink on the weekend instead of trying to stop immediately. She also recorded each day she followed the plan on a calendar. After several weeks, buying water became automatic, and she no longer wanted a sugary drink every afternoon. The experience showed that a major dietary improvement can begin with one specific, realistic change rather than a completely new diet.
key_phrases: save part of a weekly allowance
turn the choice into a habit

tasks.question: Great, some people say they have difficulty maintaining a healthy diet because they do not like the taste of healthier foods. What do you think about that argument? Why?
model_responses: I do not think healthy food has to taste unpleasant for two reasons. First, preparation methods greatly affect flavor. Vegetables can be roasted with herbs, added to soup or mixed with other ingredients instead of being served plain and overcooked. A healthy meal can include spices and different textures without depending on excessive sugar or oil. Second, people can change their habits gradually. Someone who dislikes vegetables does not need to replace every favorite dish immediately. The person can begin by adding one familiar vegetable to a meal or choosing fruit for one snack each day. Over time, repeated exposure makes new flavors feel more normal. Healthy eating is also about balance rather than eating only salads. By experimenting with preparation and making small changes, people can find nutritious foods they genuinely enjoy and maintain the diet more easily.

sets.title: Fashion and Clothing
sets.scenario_prompt: You have agreed to participate in a research study about people's experiences with fashion and clothing. You will have a short online interview with a researcher. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for signing up for the study. I'd like to ask you some questions about your experiences with fashion and clothing. First, do you enjoy shopping for clothes or is it something you find tedious? Why?
model_responses: I generally enjoy shopping for clothes, especially when I need something for a clear purpose. Trying different colors and styles can be interesting, and finding a comfortable item at a reasonable price gives me a sense of satisfaction. I usually shop with a family member or friend because another person can give honest feedback about the fit. However, I do not enjoy spending several hours walking through crowded stores without a plan. Before shopping, I check what is missing from my wardrobe and set a price limit. For example, I may decide that I need one warm jacket rather than simply looking for anything attractive. This makes the trip more efficient and reduces impulse buying. Overall, clothes shopping is enjoyable when it combines personal choice, useful advice and a practical goal instead of becoming an endless search for trends.
key_phrases: avoid an endless search for trends
shop only when something needs replacing
fit shopping into a busy schedule

tasks.question: Great, noted. Now what types of clothes do you usually prefer to wear? Do you have a particular style you enjoy?
model_responses: I usually prefer casual and comfortable clothes. On a normal school day, I wear simple T-shirts or sweaters with jeans and sneakers. I like neutral colors such as black, white, gray and blue because they are easy to combine. This means I can create several outfits from a small number of items. Comfort is important because I spend many hours sitting in class, walking between buildings and sometimes participating in activities after school. For a presentation or formal event, I choose a plain shirt, dark trousers and clean shoes so that I look organized without feeling uncomfortable. I do not follow one fashion trend closely. My style is practical, simple and easy to maintain. I prefer clothing that fits well, works in different situations and remains useful for several years.

tasks.question: Fair enough. How do you decide what to wear each day? Do you choose your clothes in the morning or the night before?
model_responses: I usually choose my clothes the night before because it makes the morning less stressful. First, I check the weather forecast. If rain is expected, I prepare shoes that will not be damaged easily and place an umbrella beside my bag. Then, I consider the next day's activities. A normal school day requires comfortable clothes, while a presentation or ceremony may require something more formal. I also make sure the items are clean and suitable for spending several hours away from home. Preparing everything at night takes only a few minutes but prevents rushed decisions when I am tired in the morning. I can wake up, get dressed and leave on time without searching for a missing item. This simple habit saves time, helps me appear prepared and allows the day to begin in a calmer way.
key_phrases: choose clothes quickly in the morning
follow a similar school schedule each day

tasks.question: Got it. And finally, some people believe that fashion trends change too quickly, and that spending money on new fashions is wasteful. Do you agree or disagree with this viewpoint? Why or why not?
model_responses: I agree that repeatedly spending money on fast-changing fashion is wasteful for two reasons. First, it harms personal finances. Trendy clothes may be worn only a few times before the style changes, so the buyer receives little long-term value. The same money could support education, savings or a durable item that remains useful for years. Second, frequent clothing purchases harm the environment. Producing fabric requires water, energy and transportation, while unwanted clothes and packaging create additional waste. People can reduce this problem by choosing simple, well-made items, combining them in different ways and repairing clothes when possible. Secondhand shopping is another practical option. Fashion can still be enjoyable without replacing an entire wardrobe each season. Buying fewer durable pieces protects both a person's budget and the environment while allowing an individual style to develop.

sets.title: Job Satisfaction
sets.scenario_prompt: You have agreed to participate in a research study about people's experiences with job satisfaction. You will have a short online interview with a researcher. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for helping with our study. I'd like to ask you some questions about your job satisfaction. First, what do you think are the most important things to consider when looking for a job?
model_responses: I think the two most important factors are opportunities for growth and a healthy work environment. First, a good job should help employees develop useful skills and take on greater responsibility over time. Training, feedback and clear promotion paths allow people to see a future in the organization rather than repeating the same basic tasks for years. Second, the workplace should be respectful and supportive. A reasonable schedule, fair manager and cooperative coworkers reduce stress and make daily work more enjoyable. Salary is important because people need financial security, but a high salary may not be enough if the job offers no learning or creates constant pressure. When looking for a position, I would therefore ask about responsibilities, training, working hours and team culture. These factors influence both long-term career development and everyday satisfaction.

tasks.question: Got it, that's helpful. Now, can you describe a job that either you or one of your friends has had? What kind of work was involved?
model_responses: One job many students are familiar with is part-time tutoring. A friend of mine tutors a younger student in mathematics and English on weekends. Before each lesson, she reviews the student's homework and test mistakes to identify weak areas. She then prepares explanations and exercises that match the student's current level. During the lesson, she uses simple examples, asks the student to explain each step and avoids giving the answer immediately. She also shares study methods that worked for her, such as keeping an error notebook, using vocabulary cards and completing timed practice. The job requires patience, communication and responsibility because one explanation may not work for every learner. Tutoring helps the younger student improve, while my friend strengthens her own knowledge and learns how personalized teaching can build confidence and independent learning habits.
key_phrases: build confidence and independent learning habits

tasks.question: Great! Moving on, what kinds of things do you think can lead people to feel unhappy in their work? Can you tell me about one or two of them?
model_responses: Two factors often make people unhappy at work. The first is an unfair or excessive workload. If employees regularly work late, receive tasks without enough time or carry more responsibility than coworkers in similar roles, they may become exhausted and resentful. The second factor is a lack of recognition and growth. People lose motivation when managers ignore good performance, provide no useful feedback and offer no opportunity to learn new skills. For example, an employee who completes difficult projects but remains in the same position for years may feel that effort has no value. Companies can address these problems by distributing work fairly, setting realistic deadlines and discussing career development regularly. Job satisfaction improves when employees have manageable responsibilities and can see that their contribution is respected and connected to future opportunities.

tasks.question: Great! And finally, some people believe that working for a large company offers more advantages than working for a small company, while others prefer the opposite. What do you think? And why?
model_responses: I would prefer to work for a large company for two reasons. First, large organizations usually provide more structured training and career opportunities. New employees may receive formal instruction, work with experienced specialists and apply for different positions within the company. This helps them develop skills and plan a long-term career. Second, large companies often offer greater stability and better benefits. They may provide reliable salaries, health insurance, paid leave and clear workplace policies. These benefits reduce financial stress and make the future more predictable. A small company may allow employees to take on varied tasks, but it may have fewer resources for training or promotion. For someone beginning a career, the support and opportunities of a large organization would be more valuable. I would therefore choose the environment that provides systematic learning and dependable employment conditions.

sets.title: Financial Planning
sets.scenario_prompt: You have volunteered for a research study about people's experiences with financial planning. You will have a short online interview with a research. The researcher will ask you some questions.

tasks.question: Thank you for joining us today to help with the study. I'd like to ask you some questions about your experiences with financial planning. First, do you currently have a financial plan or budget that you follow?
model_responses: Yes, I follow a simple monthly budget for my allowance and other small amounts of money I receive. I divide the money into three categories. About half goes into savings for larger goals, such as a new electronic device or a school trip. Thirty percent is available for daily spending, including snacks, transportation and entertainment. The remaining twenty percent is kept for books, school supplies or unexpected needs. I record purchases in a notes application and review the categories at the end of each week. If I spend too much on snacks or online shopping, I reduce that category during the following week. The plan is not complicated, but it helps me understand where my money goes. It also prevents small purchases from using money that I intended to save for something more important.

tasks.question: Thank you. If you could design the ideal way of managing your money, what would it look like?
model_responses: My ideal money-management system would have only three main parts. First, part of my allowance would move directly into savings before I could spend it. For example, I could save a fixed amount each month for a laptop or a school trip. Second, a budgeting application would automatically record my digital purchases. Instead of entering every payment by hand, I could quickly see how much I had spent on meals, transportation and entertainment. This would save time and make small expenses easier to notice. Third, I would review the information once a month and make one necessary adjustment. If I spent too much on snacks, for instance, I could lower that category the next month. A system with three clear steps would be easy for a busy student to understand, follow and maintain.
key_phrases: review the information once a month

tasks.question: I see. In your opinion, what are the most common obstacles people run into with financial planning?
model_responses: Two common obstacles are impulse spending and frequent small purchases. Impulse spending happens when people suddenly buy something they did not plan to get, perhaps because it is on sale or has attractive packaging. They can control this by waiting one day before buying a nonessential item. Small purchases are a different problem. People may deliberately buy coffee, snacks or drinks every day, but underestimate their total cost because each payment seems minor. Over a month, however, these purchases can consume a surprising part of a budget. Recording them in an application and reviewing the total each week can make the pattern visible. In short, a waiting rule helps prevent unplanned purchases, while regular tracking controls repeated everyday spending. Recognizing this difference makes financial planning clearer and more effective.
key_phrases: be influenced by a sale or attractive packaging
wait before buying a nonessential item

tasks.question: Some people believe that detailed financial planning is crucial for achieving long-term financial stability and goals. Do you agree or disagree with this belief? Why or why not?
model_responses: I agree that detailed financial planning is crucial for long-term stability for two reasons. First, a plan turns a distant goal into measurable monthly action. Someone saving for university, a laptop or future housing can calculate the amount needed and transfer part of each month's income before spending it elsewhere. This makes steady progress more likely. Second, planning prepares people for unexpected costs. Keeping emergency savings prevents a medical bill or broken device from forcing someone to borrow money or abandon another goal. A useful plan does not need to control every individual purchase, but it should identify income, major categories, savings targets and regular review dates. Without this information, people may not notice harmful spending patterns until a problem becomes serious. Financial planning therefore provides both clear direction for future goals and protection against uncertainty.
key_phrases: turn a goal into monthly action
